promotedFindings.evidence: Both Sol sessions emitted zero-token length lifecycle records adjacent to native compaction. The old collector reported preTokens=0. Recalculation after the fix reports Sol 400K compaction 86061 to 62938 tokens and Sol 1M preTokens=203228 with postTokens unknown because no valid same-settled-turn landing sample existed.

The source Opus 400K run used a transaction backup as a fold base. The product now marks only canonical, topology-valid, unique finalized applied transactions as raw archives; all timeline views retain the marker across multiple aliases, and guidance reserves raw archives for restore/rehydrate.

The two persisted Sol cells contain 4 and 9 assistant message_end events with stopReason=length, content=[], and zero input/output/cache/reasoning/total usage. A short directed-checkpoint diagnostic reproduced the same shape both before any tool call and after a successful checkpoint. The final runner classifies only the terminal assistant completion of each settled turn, preserves failed-turn tools and visible assistant evidence, skips downstream verification/judging, stores immutable matrix attempt history, and permits exactly one fresh-workspace retry.

targetedRerun.result: The raw-archive fold-base error did not recur. All three travels were on-path; P8 rebased to root and reduced active summary depth from 2 to 1.

scopeLimits: Each matrix cell and the targeted rerun are single stochastic samples; they do not estimate population-level model reliability.
Equal or different outcomes do not establish a causal hard-context-window effect.
The persisted Sol task_failure labels are superseded by post-hoc schema-v2 telemetry: both cells are provider run errors and do not support task-quality or 400K-versus-1M conclusions.

Two formal Sol 1M attempts on commit 67934f17 also ended as provider_empty_length_response before deterministic verification or judging; this supports a current provider-path reliability conclusion, not a model-capability conclusion.
The targeted rerun supports the raw-archive affordance change on the observed task; continued production-like monitoring is still required.

The broader practical ranking mixes current formal Opus evidence with earlier outcome-bearing Sol evidence and therefore ranks confidence and observed capability, not a same-commit causal model comparison.

runnerReliabilityValidation.shortRunner: provider failures are status=run_error, successful partial tools are retained, and failed excludes run errors
runnerReliabilityValidation.longFlow: failed-turn tools and transcript evidence are retained; after-turn work, deterministic verification, and judging are skipped
runnerReliabilityValidation.matrix: attemptHistory retains report/telemetry paths and SHA-256 for each attempt; run_error cells stop after two total attempts even under --retry-all
runnerReliabilityValidation.terminalSemantics: an empty zero-usage length completion is a provider error only when it is terminal for a settled turn; an internal retry that succeeds before settlement remains outcome-bearing

formalCurrentRanking.verdict: same formal tier: certifying_run, deterministic 14/14, judge 3/3 strong
formalCurrentRanking.tieBreak: Prefer 1M for operational headroom. The 400K source run chose a raw transaction archive as a fold base and expanded context, while the 1M run completed fold, root rebase, checkpoint, and rehydrate without task degradation. The corrected 400K targeted rerun also passed 3/3 strong, so this is a safety-margin preference rather than a proven quality gap.

interpretation.broaderHistoricalSignal: On commit 457fa5b3, Sol 1M was a formal certifying run with deterministic verification passed and judge 3/3 strong. Sol 400K also passed deterministic verification and received judge 3/3 strong, but was coverage_insufficient because it reached only the 30/50 pressure levels rather than the required 70 level. These are real capability signals, but commit drift and the later repeated provider failures keep them outside the current formal core-2x2 ranking.

directObservations: Opus 400K peaked at 377444 active tokens: 94.361% hard-window usage and 94.361% ACM pressure; it crossed a native compaction boundary.
Opus 1M peaked at 363149 active tokens: 36.315% hard-window usage but 90.787% ACM pressure because policy caps the working budget at 400K; it did not need native compaction.
Both windows completed the task and received 3/3 strong, so this sample does not show a reasoning-quality ceiling difference.
supportedInference: The larger hard window mainly increases recovery margin: a late or imperfect fold, failed target selection, and rehydrate round trip are less likely to collide with the hard limit.
The smaller window increases compaction pressure and makes wrong target selection materially more expensive; it rewards earlier, more accurate representation changes.
The larger window retains more raw evidence and supports deeper recovery, but it can also retain more low-attention-value sediment; size alone does not improve attention allocation.
Because both arms use a 400K working-budget policy, 1M does not postpone ACM reminders proportionally to its hard window. Hard usage and ACM pressure must be read separately.
notEstablished: A causal model-quality advantage from 1M versus 400K.
Population reliability from one stochastic sample per valid Opus arm.
Any current same-commit capability ranking for Sol from the final matrix while its provider path does not produce outcome-bearing turns.

broaderPracticalRanking.basis: Repeated 3/3 strong delivery plus the richest observed ACM repertoire: fold, root rebase, checkpoint, bounded rehydrate, and recovery from an invalid target without task degradation.

Repeated 3/3 strong delivery under near-hard-limit pressure. One source run selected a raw archive as a fold base, but the product fix and targeted rerun removed the error and again produced 3/3 strong.

An earlier outcome-bearing run was certifying and 3/3 strong, using a conservative checkpoint-heavy strategy and one precise travel. Current provider empty-length failures reduce operational confidence but are not model-quality failures.

An earlier run completed the task and judged 3/3 strong, but did not reach the required 70% pressure coverage; the later core run was contaminated by provider empty-length failures. The lower rank reflects evidence confidence and margin, not a demonstrated reasoning failure.

interpretation.excludedModels: Opus 4.6 and Terra are not ranked because the final core-2x2 did not run them to comparable, current formal outcomes.
